questions.stem: In △ABC, if 1/(a + c) + 1/(b + c) = 3/(a + b + c), show that C = 60°.
In △ABC, if a = (b − c) secθ, prove that tanθ = (2√(bc)/(b − c)) sin(A/2).
In △ABC, if a = (b + c) cosθ, prove that sinθ = (2√(bc)/(b + c)) cos(A/2).
In △ABC, if sinθ = a/(b + c), prove that cosθ = (2√(bc)/(b + c)) cos(A/2).
Show that in △ABC, tan((B − C)/2) = ((b − c)/(b + c)) cot(A/2).
In △ABC, if a : b : c = 7 : 8 : 9, find cos A : cos B : cos C.
In △ABC, prove that tan(A/2) + tan(B/2) + tan(C/2) = (bc + ca + ab − s²)/Δ.
questions.notes: Split from part ii): the two identities are separate results under one numbered question.

questions.stem: In △ABC, prove that cot(A/2) + cot(B/2) + cot(C/2) = s²/Δ.
In △ABC, prove that cot A + cot B + cot C = (a² + b² + c²)/(4Δ).
In △ABC, show that cos A/a + cos B/b + cos C/c = (a² + b² + c²)/(2abc).
In △ABC, prove that 1/r² + 1/r₁² + 1/r₂² + 1/r₃² = (a² + b² + c²)/Δ².
Show that in △ABC, a = b cos C + c cos B.
In △ABC, show that a² cot A + b² cot B + c² cot C = abc/R.
questions.notes: Star prefix runs into the cropped left gutter — two legible, a third may be cut off.

questions.stem: In △ABC, show that (b − c)² cos²(A/2) + (b + c)² sin²(A/2) = a².
In △ABC, if cot(A/2), cot(B/2), cot(C/2) are in A.P., prove that a, b, c are in A.P.
If A, A₁, A₂, A₃ are the areas of the incircle and the three excircles of a triangle respectively, prove that 1/√A₁ + 1/√A₂ + 1/√A₃ = 1/√A.
questions.notes: The book prints 'incircle and excircle ... respectively' in the singular; three excircles are meant, matching A₁, A₂, A₃.

questions.stem: If cos A + cos B + cos C = 3/2, show that the triangle is equilateral.
If tan(A/2) = 5/6 and tan(C/2) = 2/5, determine the relation between a, b and c.
If b + c = 3a, find the value of cot(B/2) cot(C/2).
In △ABC, if a = 13, b = 14, c = 15, show that R = 65/8, r = 4, r₁ = 21/2, r₂ = 12 and r₃ = 14.
In △ABC, if r₁ = 2, r₂ = 3, r₃ = 6 and r = 1, prove that a = 3, b = 4 and c = 5.
In △ABC, if r₁ = 8, r₂ = 12, r₃ = 24, find a, b and c.

If p₁, p₂, p₃ are the altitudes drawn from the vertices A, B, C to the opposite sides of a triangle, show that (i) 1/p₁ + 1/p₂ + 1/p₃ = 1/r, (ii) 1/p₁ + 1/p₂ − 1/p₃ = 1/r₃ and (iii) p₁p₂p₃ = (abc)²/(8R³).
questions.notes: Question 3 splits two levels deep: part I) carries three identities over one setup (kept as one object), part II) is a separate identity (indexed as saq3II).

questions.stem: If p₁, p₂, p₃ are the altitudes drawn from the vertices A, B, C of △ABC to the opposite sides, show that 1/p₁² + 1/p₂² + 1/p₃² = (cot A + cot B + cot C)/Δ.
questions.notes: PRINTED DEFECT: the book sets 'the centers of altitudes' where 'the lengths of the altitudes' is meant — the same p₁, p₂, p₃ as part I).

questions.stem: In △ABC, prove that (cot(A/2) + cot(B/2) + cot(C/2))/(cot A + cot B + cot C) = (a + b + c)²/(a² + b² + c²).
questions.notes: The question number and any star prefix are cropped at the left edge of the scan; numbered 4 by position between question 3 and question 5.

In △ABC, prove that r₁ + r₂ + r₃ − r = 4R.
In △ABC, prove that r + r₃ + r₁ − r₂ = 4R cos B.

In △ABC, if r₁ + r₂ = r₃ − r, show that C = 90°.

Prove that r₁(r₂ + r₃)/√(r₁r₂ + r₂r₃ + r₃r₁) = a.
